ads_ratio.reason: DATA_GAP:ads_ratio — EDGAR share counts are in ordinary shares (1,963,076,776) while the Nasdaq price ($57.10) is per ADS; per-share figures must be scaled x10 ordinary shares per ADS to be comparable to the ADS price. Note the engine's market_cap_est still multiplies the ordinary share count by the ADS price, so make_score's computed scope follows that overstated engine figure ($112.09B vs the ~$11.2B traded market cap).
ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-31, accession 0001342874-26-000020): Item 7 markets disclosure states 'Each ADS represents ten shares of Ternium S.A.'s share capital' (42,960,625 ADSs registered of record as of February 27, 2026; BNY Mellon depositary), and Selected Financial Data footnote (2) states the same ('Each ADS represents 10 shares'), with basic EPS of $0.22 per share vs $2.17 per ADS for FY2025. Corroborated by the company's own earnings releases (e.g. 4Q25: dividend $2.20 per ADS = $0.22 per share).

moat_against: Commodity product, no through-cycle pricing power: operating income fell from $5,271,136,000 in FY2021 to $705,422,000 in FY2025 (financials_history.csv) as steel prices normalized — the cycle, not Ternium, sets earnings
Global steel overcapacity and Chinese export pressure drive import competition in Mexico and Brazil; US trade measures cut both ways for a Mexican producer
Heavy, recurring capital intensity: capex rose from $1,201,639,000 (FY2023) to $2,659,101,000 (FY2025) against D&A of $788,308,000 — conservative owner's earnings were negative in FY2025

Usiminas overhang leaks and whipsaws earnings: large noncontrolling interests, a $405M deferred-tax-asset writedown and a recurring litigation provision over the Usiminas participation acquisition in FY2025 (company 4Q25 release)
FX and country exposure: MXN/BRL/ARS earnings, Argentine macro and controls, and Brazilian tax/litigation risk sit outside management's control
moat_for: Regional leadership: leading flat-steel producer in Mexico and Argentina and, via Usiminas (consolidated July 2023), Brazil — scale, integrated iron-ore mining and plants close to manufacturing customers give logistics and availability advantages importers cannot match at distance

Value-added differentiation: galvanized, painted and automotive/industrial products plus a service-center network and the ProPymes SME program embed Ternium in customer supply chains beyond plain hot-rolled coil

Balance-sheet capacity to invest through the cycle: engine net debt $887,783,000 at FY2025 on its cash-only definition (the company reported a $712M net cash position including financial securities at Dec 31, 2025) while funding the Pesquería expansion, the largest in its history
moat_justification: Leading flat-steel producer in Mexico and Argentina (plus Brazil via Usiminas, consolidated since July 2023) with integrated iron-ore mining, a dense service-center/distribution network and a value-added mix — real regional scale, logistics and customer-embedding advantages. But the product is commodity flat steel with no through-cycle pricing power: operating income fell from $5,271M (FY2021) to $705M (FY2025) on the filed history as steel prices normalized, conservative owner's earnings were negative in FY2025 at peak Pesquería growth capex, and earnings are set by steel prices, Chinese export pressure, FX and Argentine/Brazilian macro that Ternium does not control. Weak-to-moderate moat, 4/10, CAP 7.2y.
name: Ternium S.A.
one_liner: Leading Latin-American flat-steel producer, weak-to-moderate moat 4/10 — on the normalized conservative base (median OE $0.43 per ADS across the peak Pesquería capex years) the price is far beyond the model: weighted IRR 3.14% (bear cases at the solver floor, so at most ~3%), weighted IV@15% $3.03 vs $57.10 per ADS, Tier D, and even the super-bull case returns only 3.91%; clears 15% only below ~$3.03 on this base.

sbc_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction: the engine has no filed SBC value for Ternium in any period (last_filed_value is null), so any override flags out-of-band. The value is not an estimate and has no filed anchor to be a multiple of — it is the filer's own reported position (no share-based payment line exists in its 20-F cash-flow statement; see source).
sbc_override.reason: DATA_GAP:sbc — SBC missing for fiscal years 2023, 2024, 2025 under every tag the engine reads (ifrs-full AdjustmentsForSharebasedPayments / ExpenseFromSharebasedPaymentTransactionsWithEmployees have no facts in this filer's companyfacts for any year 2016-2025). Ternium has no equity-settled share-based payment expense to subtract: it files no IFRS 2 expense and its sole incentive program is cash-settled and already inside operating cash flow — subtracting it again as SBC would double-count it. The filing-sourced figure for equity SBC in the gap years is $0 (same treatment as TS in this sweep).
sbc_override.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-31, accession 0001342874-26-000020), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (p. F-11): the adjustments reconciling profit to operating cash flow for 2025, 2024 and 2023 are enumerated in full (depreciation and amortization, impairment charge, income tax accruals less payments, equity in earnings of non-consolidated companies, interest accruals, provisions and working-capital changes) with no share-based payment addback in any year, and the term 'share-based' appears nowhere in the 20-F. The only long-term incentive (Item 6 / Note 4(o)(3) and Note 26(iii)) grants units that are mandatorily redeemed for cash seven years after grant, are tied to book value, and are accounted for as an IAS 19 long-term benefit (liability $84.7M at Dec 31, 2025) — cash-settled, already expensed through income and operating cash flow; directors receive cash only, with 'no long-term incentive or pension plan'.

shares_override.reason: DATA_GAP:shares — DILUTED shares missing for fiscal years 2023, 2024, 2025 of the last 3; EDGAR carries only the non-diluted WeightedAverageShares count (1,963,076,776 in each year), which the engine records as a fallback and refuses to silently swap. The filer's own 20-F states diluted EPS equals basic EPS, so the diluted count is the same 1,963,076,776 the filer itself uses for both — the override is exact for all three gap years, not an approximation, because the count was unchanged in every year.
shares_override.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-31, accession 0001342874-26-000020), Consolidated Statements of Income (p. F-6): 'Weighted average number of shares outstanding 1,963,076,776' for each of 2025, 2024 and 2023, with the line captioned 'Basic and diluted earnings per share for profit attributable to the owners of the parent (expressed in $ per share) 0.22 / (0.03) / 0.34'; Selected Financial Data footnote (4) states 'Diluted earnings per share and per ADS (expressed in $ per share or ADS), equals basic earnings per share or ADS, respectively', and accounting policy Note (x) calculates EPS on the daily weighted average number of ordinary shares excluding treasury shares (41,666,666 held in treasury).
